The transparent goby Aphia minuta is a small, short-lived marine teleost that exhibits several distinctive life-history traits typical of a fast-paced pelagic existence. Field surveys indicate that the ultimate total length attained by adults is 7.9 centimeters [Li = 7.9 centimeters], a modest maximum size that positions this species among the smallest gobiids in the Mediterranean and adjacent Atlantic waters. At the onset of reproductive activity, individuals measure approximately 3.8 centimeters [Lp = approximately 3.8 centimeters] in total length, reflecting a relatively early maturation schedule given their short lifespan. The wet weight at puberty, reported as 0.3249 grams [Wwp = 0.3249 grams], was derived from length-weight regressions calibrated for gobiid fishes and is consistent with the small body plan of this pelagic species. These morphometric parameters underscore an overall life-history strategy that prioritizes rapid maturation and early reproduction over extended somatic growth.

Reproductive output in Aphia minuta has been characterized under controlled thermal conditions that approximate its native habitat. At a stable temperature of 10 °C [T = 10 °C], females display an estimated maximum daily egg production rate that translates to roughly 7.3 eggs per day [Ri = roughly 7.3 eggs per day], a value that reflects the species' iteroparous, batch-spawning mode. In more naturalistic terms, this daily rate arises from females producing several hundred eggs per spawning event [N_R_i = several hundred eggs per spawning event] and spawning multiple times over the course of the season [F_R_i = multiple times over the course of the season], though direct field verification of clutch frequency remains limited. The overall annual reproductive effort is nevertheless substantial relative to body size, indicating that a large proportion of acquired energy is channeled into gamete production during the relatively brief reproductive window.

The very earliest life stages of the transparent goby are characterized by rapid embryogenesis and a small initial body mass. Eggs maintained at 12 °C [T = 12 °C] complete development and hatch after approximately 12 days [ab = approximately 12 days], a brief incubation period consistent with the warm-water, fast-growth strategy of this pelagic species. The wet weight at birth is minute, estimated at 0.0002771 grams [Wwb = 0.0002771 grams], a value based on egg dimensions typical of related gobiids and reflecting the energetically lean yolk reserves available to the non-feeding, yolk-sac larva after eclosion. This extremely small birth mass imposes a narrow window for the larva to successfully initiate exogenous feeding before endogenous reserves are exhausted, making the period following hatching a critical bottleneck for survival.

Lifespan constraints in this species are pronounced and help define its overall demographic profile. The maximum recorded life span of 365 days [am = 365 days] under environmental temperatures averaging 10 °C [T = 10 °C] confirms its status as a strictly annual fish in most wild populations, a duration that, while brief, is typical of many small, fast-living gobiids and is strongly influenced by seasonal food availability and predation pressure. The ultimate wet weight of adults reaches 3.11 grams [Wwi = 3.11 grams], a value that underscores the small body size this species maintains throughout its brief existence and that likely influences its vulnerability to predation and its role in pelagic food webs. The combination of early maturation, high reproductive output, and complete adult turnover on an annual cycle places Aphia minuta at the extreme fast end of the life-history continuum among teleosts.

Comparative morphometric data place the transparent goby among the smaller members of the Gobiidae, and its life-history parameters align closely with those of other pelagic, short-lived planktivores. The asymptotic adult mass of 3.11 grams [Wwi = 3.11 grams] stands in stark contrast to the initial birth mass, reflecting a more than ten-thousand-fold increase during development. Adults attain a maximum total length of 7.9 cm [Li = 7.9 cm], a dimension that places this species among the smallest gobiids. Hatching occurs after an incubation period of about 12 days [ab = about 12 days] at 12 °C [T = 12 °C], and the maximum longevity of 365 days [am = 365 days] at 10 °C [T = 10 °C] reinforces the annual life cycle typical of this ruderal strategist in coastal pelagic ecosystems.
